notes: Units: workspace budget at session start was 800,000 with 603,481 already used (196,519 remaining). This research used approximately 38,545 units, leaving roughly 157,974 (see unitsUsed/unitsRemaining below - pulled from a final subscription-info-limits-and-usage check).

IMPORTANT DISCREPANCY: the measured Tier-1 destination cluster (10 head terms × 10 markets) totals 167,430/month, far below the 825,000/month baseline in the handoff brief. We could not reproduce or substantiate 825,000/month from Ahrefs for the destination cluster as scoped (10 keywords x 9-10 languages). Possible explanations: the baseline may have summed many more destination/city variants per country (e.g. per-city or per-network keyword lists), used a broader match/estimation method, or is simply an unverified planning estimate. Treat 825,000 as an unverified planning number, not a re-confirmed figure.

Given the gap above, reaching the 2,000,000-3,000,000/month target is NOT substantiated by this research at the current keyword scope. The realistic measured addressable universe (10 clusters x 18 markets, real Ahrefs volumes only) is 441,340/month. Adding a single sampled long-tail expansion (5 head terms, matching-terms, en-us only) adds 448,720/month more, taking the total to 890,060/month - and that long tail is dominated by generic/branded/informational queries ("esim" itself, iPhone esim troubleshooting, branded competitor names) rather than clean commercial destination/travel intent. Reaching 2-3M/month would require replicating that matching-terms long-tail expansion across most or all 18 markets (not just en-us), which this budget did not cover - recommend a follow-up pass with matching-terms run per-market on the top 3-5 head terms per market if that ceiling number is needed with real data.

Ahrefs keywords-explorer-overview omits rows entirely for keywords it has no tracked data for in a given country, rather than returning volume=0. We only include keywords Ahrefs actually returned data for. Missing-keyword counts per market (out of 53 submitted per market, 52 for ar-sa): de-de 7, fr-fr 7, it-it 10, es-es 8, nl-nl 8, pl-pl 17, pt-pt 18, ro-ro 29, ja-jp 11, ko-kr 14, zh-Hant-tw 16, tr-tr 14, ar-ae 38, ar-sa 34, id-id 16, ru-ru 16 (en-us and en-gb: 0 missing, all 53 returned). These gaps are NOT volume=0 - they are 'no Ahrefs data', mostly in the smaller/less-common clusters (vs_alternatives, airport, bridge) and in thinner-coverage markets (ro-ro, ar-ae, ar-sa). A handful of keywords Ahrefs did return came back with volume=null despite other metadata present (e.g. 'esim oder lokale sim' in de-de, 'esim 數據方案' in zh-Hant-tw, 'număr virtual' in ro-ro, 'أفضل esim' in ar-ae) - these are included in the keywords array with volume:null and excluded from all totals, per instructions to never invent a volume.

Arabic markets (ar-ae, ar-sa) show almost no measurable demand for our translated term set in Ahrefs (ae: 100/mo across 14 returned keywords; sa: 210/mo across 18 returned keywords), against 38 and 34 missing keywords respectively. This looks like a genuine Ahrefs coverage gap for Arabic eSIM terminology as much as low real demand - the generic 'esim' head term alone showed ae=5,300/mo and sa=4,000/mo in the volume-by-country pull, which is real but did not carry through to our specific translated long-form phrases. Verdict: research further with native-speaker keyword discovery before concluding 'skip' - we've downgraded both to 'skip' based on the data we could get, but flag this as the weakest-confidence verdict in the set.

Mainland China (zh-Hans, cn) was not measured. Ahrefs' country list has no 'cn' entries in any of our volume-by-country pulls (confirmed via the generic 'esim' by-country breakdown, which lists tw, hk but never cn) - Ahrefs does not track Baidu/mainland search volume, so zh-Hans/China demand is fundamentally unmeasurable with this tool. Any China plan needs a separate data source (Baidu Index, 5118, etc).

Brazil (pt-br) was not measured; only pt-pt (Portugal) was, as specified as the primary option in the brief. Portugal shows real but modest volume (2,220/mo across 35 keywords) with 18 keywords missing entirely - Brazil is very likely a much larger market for Portuguese-language eSIM content given its population and outbound travel volume, and should be measured separately before ruling Portuguese in or out at scale.

Russia (ru-ru) 'build' verdict is heavily driven by one bridge-cluster generic term, 'виртуальный номер' (virtual number) at 20,000/mo, which is not an eSIM-specific query - it's a generic virtual-number search relevant mainly to the future Livdar phone-number bridge product, not core eSIM demand. Excluding that one term, measured ru-ru volume is 7,580/mo. There is also a standing access/monetization caveat for the Russian market noted in the brief that this research does not evaluate.

Taiwan (zh-Hant-tw) volume is dominated by 'esim 設定' (esim settings, 16,000/mo, setup cluster) and 'esim 日本' (esim japan, 30,000/mo, destination cluster) - both plausible and real but concentrated in two terms; the rest of the Taiwan keyword set is thin.

Long-tail matching-terms sampling was run for only 5 head terms (esim, esim turkey, buy esim, travel sim card, iphone esim), all in en-us, per the 'sparingly, 3-5 head terms' instruction. It was not run in any other market. The iphone esim long tail is largely device-support/troubleshooting queries (how to transfer/delete/activate esim on various iPhone models) which have real volume but weak commercial/travel intent for an eSIM storefront - treat that portion as content/SEO opportunity, not direct conversion opportunity.

clusterTotals and marketTotals only sum rows with a non-null volume; keywords with volume:null are still listed in the keywords array (per 'never invent a volume, put null') but excluded from every total and from the expansion figures.

Airport/arrival cluster volume is very low everywhere we measured it (Tier 1 total: 100/mo; Tier 2 total: 810/mo) - named-airport queries (e.g. 'sim card jfk airport', 'esim at airport') returned mostly 0 or missing. This looks like a genuinely small cluster in Ahrefs' data, not a measurement gap - people searching for airport SIM/eSIM options appear to phrase it differently than we tested (e.g. as part of broader 'airport wifi' or city-specific queries), so this cluster may be undercounted rather than actually small; would need broader phrasing research to confirm.

vs_alternatives cluster (esim vs sim card, esim vs roaming, etc.) is consistently the smallest measured cluster (Tier 1: 1,500/mo; Tier 2: 290/mo) across every market - this looks like a real, low-value cluster for keyword targeting, better handled as supporting content within destination/setup pages rather than as standalone target pages.
